messages:
erin: Quick thought — control-plane <-> runtime handshake is getting heavy across hosted / dedicated / private. I want a tiny, explicit "capability shim" that lists only the features runtime must honor (routing, kv-cache, quant profiles) + a separate network/policy mapping. WDYT?

jon: example of the shape? is this just a subset of the existing manifest?

erin: yeah but normalized. minimal fields: 
- capabilities: [streaming, kv_cache, quantized] 
- fallbacks: [compatible_model_tags] 
- network: {allowed_subnets, egress_policy} 

alex: if we go that route we should make the network mapping optional for hosted. For private, it must carry KMS endpoints + CIDR. Sketch:

```json
{
  "capabilities": ["streaming","kv_cache"],
  "network": {"type": "vpc", "cidrs": ["10.0.0.0/16"], "kms_endpoint": "https://kms.corp"},
  "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

liz: caveat — we cannot transmit customer KMS keys or plaintext endpoints to hosted. private can include reference-only metadata (e.g., kms_region) but not credentials. otherwise compliance flags.

kevin: agree. also need a clear fallback policy for when capability mismatch occurs. proposal: three-tier fallback: 
1) best-effort feature degrade (e.g., disable streaming)
2) route to compatible model variant in same region
3) return 5xx + actionable error for client to retry with different hint

rebecca: also add a "manifest_version" and a compatibility bitmap so runtimes can quickly check. versioning will help rollouts and A/B with Dedicated.

erin: +1 on versioning and fallback tiers. action items:
- I will draft a tiny RFC with the minimal json schema (capabilities, network_hint, fallback_policy, version)
- @alex to prototype translation layer that maps old manifest -> shim (week 1)
- @liz to enumerate compliance constraints for private shims (list of forbidden fields)
- @kevin to draft fallback semantics and error codes

infra-bot: Note: created issue INF-4123 "capability-shim-proposal" and assigned to erin. :white_check_mark:

jon: thanks — please add a simple example where hosted returns "network_hint": null and private returns a region-only hint. saves headaches.

erin: will do. planning a 30m sync Friday; will post calendar invite.

alex: nit — include a "trust_level" enum (hosted|dedicated|private) so runtimes can short-circuit policy checks in fast-path.

liz: +1 for trust_level. we'll map it to allowed telemetry & audit granularity in the RFC.

erin: cool. thanks everyone. short RFC + prototype next week.
